The strongest evidence is uneven across domains: clear improvement in macro indicators, much weaker or mixed movement on housing, Gaza accountability, and some domestic implementation problems.","evidence":[{"title":"Employment Situation News Release - 2024 M04 Results","publisher":"U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics","date":"2024-05-03","url":"https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_05032024.htm","summary":"April payrolls rose by 175,000 and unemployment was 3.9%, which is directionally consistent with Biden’s repeated “middle-class/jobs” claim, though still partly the result of broader post-pandemic normalization.","question_ids":["8B.7","8B.1","8B.2"]},{"title":"Employment Situation News Release - 2024 M07 Results","publisher":"U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics","date":"2024-08-02","url":"https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_08022024.htm","summary":"July unemployment rose to 4.3% but payrolls still increased by 114,000, which is weaker than spring 2024 but still not a labor-market collapse; this supports a soft-landing reading more than a failure reading.","question_ids":["8B.7"]},{"title":"Consumer Price Index Summary, June 2024","publisher":"U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics","date":"2024-07-11","url":"https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/cpi_07112024.htm","summary":"CPI-U fell 0.1% in June and was up 3.0% over 12 months, so inflation was moving in the direction Biden said he sought, even if housing remained sticky.","question_ids":["8B.7","8B.1"]},{"title":"Gross Domestic Product, Second Quarter 2024 (Advance Estimate)","publisher":"U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis","date":"2024-07-25","url":"https://www.bea.gov/news/2024/gross-domestic-product-second-quarter-2024-advance-estimate","summary":"Real GDP grew at a 2.8% annual rate in Q2 2024, which is consistent with the administration’s claim of a resilient economy and not a recessionary outcome.","question_ids":["8B.7","8B.1"]},{"title":"Joint Statement of Janet L.
